source: Committee on Tactical Combat Casualty Care (CoTCCC)
description: TCCC protocols for trauma management in high-threat environments - adapted from military TCCC for civilian first responders

actions: Move casualty to cover if possible
Apply tourniquet for life-threatening hemorrhage (massive extremity bleeding)
Immediate tourniquet application only
Move to Tactical Field Care when safe

protocols.threat: No active hostile fire or reduced threat

actions: Apply tourniquet 2-3 inches above bleeding site (not over joints)
Tighten until bleeding stops
Mark with 'T' and time
If junctional (groin/axilla/neck): use hemostatic gauze with pressure
Open airway with jaw thrust
Clear visible obstructions
Advanced airway only if trained and equipment available
Consider nasopharyngeal airway (9.0-9.5 French for adults, 6.0 for children)
Do NOT attempt surgical cricothyrotomy unless trained
contraindications: Suspected skull base fracture - use oropharyngeal only

actions: Needle decompression for tension pneumothorax (2nd intercostal, midclavicular line)
Seal open/sucking chest wounds with vented chest seal
Consider chest tube if trained and equipment available
Monitor for respiratory distress
Establish IV/IO access if hypovolemic shock present
Fluid resuscitation: Hypotensive resuscitation (SBP ~90mmHg)
Preferred: 1-2L Normal Saline or Lactated Ringer's wide open
Avoid over-resuscitation (can dislodge clots)
Consider whole blood if available (preferred)

interventions: Treat hypoglycemia if present (oral glucose or IV D50)

actions: Fully expose casualty (cut clothes)
Prevent hypothermia
Use warm blankets/heating devices
Minimize time on cold ground

tranexamic_acid.dose: 1g IV/IO over 10 minutes, then 1g over 8 hours

protocols.setting: During evacuation to higher echelon care
interventions: Blood product transfusion if available (preferred 1:1:1 ratio)
Maintain permissive hypotension (SBP 80-90mmHg) until surgical control
Consider REBOA if available and trained
protocols.transfer_criteria: Transfer to trauma center with surgical capabilities

principles: Do the greatest good for the greatest number
Minimal care to save most lives

immediate.criteria: Life-threatening injuries, salvageable with immediate care
immediate.interventions: Airway control, tourniquet, needle decompression, rapid transport

delayed.criteria: Serious injuries, can wait for care
delayed.interventions: Standard trauma care when resources available

expectant.criteria: Deceased or mortally injured, not salvageable
expectant.interventions: Comfort care only, may be used as last resort for resources

protocols.triage_algorithm: SALT Triage - Sort, Assess, Lifesaving interventions, Treatment/transport

pediatric.airway: Smaller equipment, higher risk of obstruction

pregnant.positioning: Left lateral tilt if >20 weeks gestation

geriatric.medications: Reduced dosing, monitor for side effects
